the distribution of references across a citing article and the number of times that a cited work is cited in a citing article both influence the citation rankings of works.

the results of the analysis of the citation network are not necessarily the same as the results obtained by the analysis of a citation network.

the distribution of citations across the citing text is an important factor in determining how much a reference contributes to the citing article.
the citation counts of a paper are highly dependent upon the context of the paper.
